perf.summary: Update duplicates child pointer loads/null-checks across Size() and Sum() helpers for both children.
perf.currentCost: 4 loads + 4 null compares per Update, on every Merge/SplitBySize frame.
perf.proposedChange: Cache `TreapImplicitNode* l = n->Left, r = n->Right;` once; derive size and sum from the cached pointers.
perf.rationale: Halves redundant loads/branches; Size and Sum of a child sit in one cache line so the fused read is near-free after the first deref.

perf.summary: ApplyLazy computes (long)n->Size * lazy with a sign-extending widening of an int that is always >= 1; fine, but the n->Lazy += lazy / HasLazy = true store happens even when accumulating onto a node that will be immediately overwritten by a deeper push. Minor: the cast is correct and needed.
perf.currentCost: One int->long widen + multiply + two stores per lazy application. Correct as-is.
perf.proposedChange: Keep the cast (it is required to avoid 32-bit overflow). No change to math. Optional: mark struct field ordering so HasLazy/Rev bytes pack (see layout opportunity) to keep Lazy/Sum on one line with Value for this read-modify-write.
perf.rationale: The arithmetic is already minimal; the only real lever here is struct packing addressed separately. Listing to confirm the (long) cast must stay.
perf.risk: Removing the (long) cast would overflow for Size*lazy beyond 2^31 — do NOT remove it.

perf.summary: Two separate bool fields (Rev, HasLazy) placed before the 8-byte-aligned pointers force 6+ bytes of padding; the struct is larger than necessary, hurting cache density of the node pool.
perf.currentCost: Layout (Sequential): int Priority(4), int Size(4), long Value(8), long Sum(8), long Lazy(8), bool Rev(1), bool HasLazy(1) -> 6 bytes pad to align Left -> Left(8), Right(8). Total 56B but with the two bools costing an aligned 8B slot. On a 64B line, fewer nodes per line than needed.
perf.proposedChange: Pack the two bools into a single byte flags field (bit0=Rev, bit1=HasLazy), or at minimum group both bools adjacent (already are) and move them to the very end after Right so the trailing pad is shared. Combining into one `byte Flags` removes one bool's footprint and lets Push test/set bits with masks.
perf.rationale: Smaller node -> more nodes per cache line -> fewer misses during the pointer-chasing Merge/Split. Bit flags also let Push check 'any lazy work pending' with a single nonzero test instead of two bool loads.
perf.risk: Changes field layout / public struct ABI. Bitwise flag access must preserve exact toggle semantics (Rev = !Rev becomes Flags ^= REV_BIT). Acceptable only if no external code reads .Rev/.HasLazy directly. Burst-blittable preserved.
